jurisdiction.name: Poland
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Poland implements the EU AI Act through the Act of 3 July 2026 on AI systems, in force since August 2026, which creates the Commission for the Development and Safety of AI (KRiBSI) as market surveillance authority and provides an AI regulatory sandbox. National policy still rests on the Council of Ministers' 2020 AI Policy; its 2030 successor is a draft resolution. The Ministry of Digital Affairs has issued an AI guide for public administration and draft model AI contract clauses, the Ministry of National Defence has an AI strategy to 2039, and the data protection authority (UODO) and the financial supervisor (KNF) issued AI guidance in 2026. In August 2026 the Prime Minister's Order No. 46 created a Department of AI Development and Security in the Ministry of Digital Affairs.
lead_institutions: Commission for the Development and Safety of AI (KRiBSI)
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The updated AI Policy to 2030 is still a draft and is recorded as one. A further browser check on 22 October 2026 added records from official sources.

instruments.official_title: Ustawa z dnia 3 lipca 2026 r. o systemach sztucznej inteligencji
instruments.english_title: Act of 3 July 2026 on Artificial Intelligence Systems
instruments.issuing_authority: Sejm of the Republic of Poland (Parliament; Act signed and promulgated in Dziennik Ustaw 2026 poz. 1003)
instruments.publisher_name: Sejm of the Republic of Poland
instruments.current_status: In force (status 'obowiązujący' on eli.gov.pl). Dated 3 July 2026, published in Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1003 on 27 July 2026, entered into force 11 August 2026; art. 125(4) applied from 28 July 2026 and arts. 8-18 and chapters 3-5, 8 and 9 apply from 28 October 2026. The Sejm appointed the first KRiBSI Chair on 18 September 2026 with Senate consent of 24 September 2026 (M.P. 2026 poz. 945 and 946). Responsible minister: minister competent for computerisation.
instruments.summary: Poland's national implementing law for the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689): it sets up the Commission for the Development and Security of Artificial Intelligence (KRiBSI) as market surveillance authority and single point of contact, the procedure for infringements, accreditation and notification of conformity-assessment bodies, AI-development support measures and administrative fines. It establishes a KRiBSI-run AI regulatory sandbox (6-12 months, entry by competition), excludes national defence, special services and pre-market research, and amends ten acts including the personal data protection, financial-market supervision, broadcasting and national cybersecurity system acts.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Poland's AI Act implementing law and founding instrument of the national AI supervisor KRiBSI.

instruments.official_title: Polityka rozwoju sztucznej inteligencji w Polsce do 2030 roku
instruments.english_title: Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland until 2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Affairs (draft for adoption by the Council of Ministers)
instruments.current_status: Not yet adopted. The Ministry of Digital Affairs published this updated version on 17 November 2025 after public consultation; on 16 April 2026 it published the draft Council of Ministers resolution establishing the policy (project ID260, documents dated 15 April 2026), which would repeal Resolution No. 196 of 2020, and sent it for opinions and inter-ministerial agreement (https://www.gov.pl/web/cyfryzacja/projekt-uchwaly-rady-ministrow-w-sprawie-ustanowienia-polityki-rozwoju-sztucznej-inteligencji-w-polsce-do-2030-roku-id260). No adopting resolution was found in Monitor Polski (Sejm ELI search) as of 12 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Updated draft national AI policy to 2030, revised after public consultation, organised in four pillars: the Polish AI ecosystem (infrastructure incl. AI Factories and the planned Baltic AI GigaFactory, open data and the PLLuM model, science and skills), an efficient state (AI HUB Poland platform, AI in public services), 'Heart of the AI Continent' (key sectors with sectoral deployment maps, SME support, regulatory sandboxes) and trustworthy AI (regulation and ethics, data protection, consumer and copyright protection). It adds product and result indicators and puts implementation under the minister for computerisation with oversight and reporting to the Committee for Digital Affairs.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Successor national AI strategy in preparation; would replace the 2020 AI Policy.

instruments.official_title: Resortowa strategia sztucznej inteligencji do roku 2039
instruments.english_title: Departmental Artificial Intelligence Strategy until 2039 (Ministry of National Defence)
instruments.current_status: Introduced into service use in the defence department (ministry page dated 11 October 2024; document dated August 2024). Current departmental strategy.
instruments.summary: Strategy of the national defence department (resort obrony narodowej) for responsible and scalable adoption of AI in the Polish Armed Forces up to 2039. It diagnoses the department's AI readiness, sets a 2039 vision, weighs military AI opportunities and threats, and sets three operational goals (preparing for AI implementation, scalable deployment, protection of strategic assets and solutions) with intervention directions and recommendations on organisational culture, skills, ICT infrastructure and R&D.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Defence-sector AI strategy; defence is outside the scope of the AI systems Act.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Affairs (applicant), submitted to the Committee for Digital Affairs
instruments.current_status: Draft government document submitted by the Vice-Chair of the Committee for Digital Affairs on 16 February 2026 for review (comments due 20 February 2026) and placed on the agenda of the Committee's 27 February 2026 meeting; comments from ZUS, MSWiA and KPRM and the ministry's reply are published. instruments.summary: Draft standard contract provisions for public-administration buyers acquiring, building, deploying, maintaining and developing AI systems that are not high-risk under the EU AI Act. The clauses cover AI-specific issues such as transparency, data governance, human oversight, robustness and cybersecurity, drawing on EU model clauses and Polish public-procurement law; high-risk and general-purpose AI systems are expressly left out.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Model AI procurement clauses for the public sector.

instruments.official_title: Przewodnik po sztucznej inteligencji dla administracji publicznej
instruments.english_title: Guide to Artificial Intelligence for Public Administration
instruments.current_status: Launched on 5 March 2026 at a nationwide meeting with local-government units, together with a national free training programme for officials (Ministry of Digital Affairs announcement 'Premiera pierwszego przewodnika po AI dla urzędów', https://www.gov.pl/web/cyfryzacja/premiera-pierwszego-przewodnika-po-ai-dla-urzedow). Described as an open document to be updated.
instruments.summary: Ministry of Digital Affairs guide helping public administration staff use generative AI safely and responsibly. In five parts (AI basics; legal and ethical framework; implementing AI in practice; risks and limitations; tools and resources) it covers planning, deploying and testing AI in offices, requirements under the EU AI Act and GDPR with emphasis on real human oversight, and rules for officials using generative tools, including hallucination risks and verifying outputs before use in official documents.

instruments.english_title: Resolution No. 196 of the Council of Ministers of 28 December 2020 establishing the "Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland from 2020"
instruments.current_status: Adopted 28 December 2020, published in Monitor Polski on 12 January 2021, effective 13 January 2021 (eli.gov.pl: 'akt jednorazowy'). Still the adopted AI policy: the draft Council of Ministers resolution on the AI Policy to 2030 (ID260, 15 April 2026) would repeal it, but no adopting resolution was found in Monitor Polski as of 12 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers resolution establishing Poland's first national AI policy (the 'AI Policy'), annexed to the resolution in Monitor Polski 2021 poz. 23. It names the minister competent for computerisation as executor and requires an annual report to the Council of Ministers on implementation by 1 September each year. The policy sets objectives for society, innovative companies, science, education, international cooperation and the public sector.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Poland's national AI strategy currently in force; to be replaced by the AI Policy to 2030 (the draft resolution repeals Resolution No. 196).

instruments.official_title: Listy pytań inicjalnych – Ochrona danych osobowych w kontekście systemów sztucznej inteligencji
instruments.english_title: Initial question lists – Personal data protection in the context of artificial intelligence systems
instruments.issuing_authority: Personal Data Protection Office (UODO), prepared with its Social Expert Team
instruments.current_status: Published on the UODO website on 6 August 2026 (cover letter dated 5 August 2026); UODO invited comments to pytania_inicjalne@uodo.gov.pl until 30 September 2026.
instruments.summary: UODO's four GDPR checklists for organisations to answer before building or using an AI system: a version for SMEs using off-the-shelf AI tools, one for public-sector bodies (reflecting legality and administrative-procedure rules), a 'Version 0' for others including those building or fine-tuning models, and an extended list that also flags EU AI Act duties such as risk classification and fundamental-rights impact assessment. UODO states they do not replace a risk analysis or DPIA, are not a binding interpretation and need not be submitted to the authority.

instruments.official_title: Rekomendacje dla podmiotów rynku finansowego dotyczące wpływu modeli Frontier AI na cyberbezpieczeństwo
instruments.english_title: Recommendations for financial market entities on the impact of frontier AI models on cybersecurity
instruments.issuing_authority: Office of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (UKNF)
instruments.current_status: Published on knf.gov.pl with update date 22 July 2026, alongside a CSIRT KNF note 'Wpływ rozwoju modeli AI na dynamikę zagrożeń' (23 July 2026).
instruments.summary: UKNF recommendations telling financial institutions to reassess ICT risk in light of frontier AI models that can speed up vulnerability discovery and automate attacks. Under DORA they should build AI threats into ICT risk management (new attack scenarios, staff training on AI phishing and deepfakes), include AI-enabled attacks in digital resilience testing, prioritise vulnerabilities by real risk, address risks of AI agents, permissions and dependence on AI service providers, and make boards assess frontier AI's effect on the risk profile.

instruments.current_status: Signed 25 August 2026 and published in Monitor Polski on 26 August 2026 (poz. 876); it enters into force on the day after publication.
instruments.summary: Amends the statute of the Ministry of Digital Affairs, annexed to Order No. 661 of 29 December 2023, to create a new organisational unit, the Department of Artificial Intelligence Development and Security (Departament Rozwoju i Bezpieczeństwa Sztucznej Inteligencji). The order adds the department to sections 2 and 3 of the statute; it does not set out the department's tasks.

instruments.official_title: Stanowisko Urzędu Komisji Nadzoru Finansowego w sprawie świadczenia usługi robo-doradztwa
instruments.english_title: Position of the Office of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority on the provision of robo-advice services
instruments.issuing_authority: Office of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (UKNF)
instruments.current_status: Published 4 November 2020; the position states it is not a source of law but an explanation of the applicable provisions, and that later legal changes may affect it.
instruments.summary: Supervisory position for investment firms and banks providing investment advice through algorithms (robo-advice). It expects documented algorithm design and changes, testing of methodology and data (not only technical function), protection of algorithms against unauthorised access, prompt correction of algorithm errors, regular monitoring, disclosure of algorithms' limits and risks to clients, and involvement of competent staff and compliance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Financial supervisor's expectations on algorithm-based (robo-advice) investment advice.

instruments.official_title: Chat GPT w szkole. Szanse i zagrożenia
instruments.english_title: ChatGPT at school: opportunities and risks
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Education and Science (Ministerstwo Edukacji i Nauki)
instruments.current_status: Published by the Ministry of Education and Science on 24 April 2023 (page 'Chat GPT – materiał dla nauczycieli', now kept in the 2021-2023 Ministry of Education and Science news archive on the Ministry of Science and Higher Education site) with the PDF 'Chat GPT w szkole - szanse i zagrożenia'. The PDF carries no printed date; its copyright holder is the Educational Research Institute. Followed by the November 2023 guide 'Do czego AI nie służy'. The Ministry's page for that November 2023 guide refers to the earlier material as published in July 2023.
instruments.summary: Article for teachers on ChatGPT and generative AI in schools, written for the Educational Research Institute (IBE) and published by the Ministry of Education and Science as the first output of its 'AI w Edukacji' working group. It explains what AI and ChatGPT are, whether ChatGPT is dangerous, how to use it wisely in teaching, how to check who wrote a piece of work, and how it can support learners with special needs.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National education ministry guidance for teachers on generative AI use in schools.

organizations.name: Sejm of the Republic of Poland
organizations.ai_governance_role: Lower house of the Polish Parliament; enacted the Act of 3 July 2026 on AI systems (with the Senate) and appoints, with Senate consent, the Chair of the Commission for the Development and Security of Artificial Intelligence (KRiBSI).

organizations.name: Ministry of Digital Affairs
organizations.ai_governance_role: Minister competent for computerisation (informatyzacja); lead ministry for AI policy: executor of the 2020 AI Policy, author of the draft AI Policy to 2030, the AI guide for public administration and the draft model AI contract clauses, and the minister responsible for the AI systems Act (houses the KRiBSI support unit).

organizations.name: Council of Ministers
organizations.ai_governance_role: Polish government; adopted the AI Policy from 2020 (Resolution No. 196 of 28 December 2020) and is to adopt the AI Policy to 2030 by resolution (draft ID260).

organizations.name: Ministry of National Defence
organizations.ai_governance_role: Issued the departmental AI strategy to 2039 for the national defence sector, which is excluded from the scope of the AI systems Act.

organizations.name: Committee for Digital Affairs
organizations.ai_governance_role: Council of Ministers auxiliary body (Komitet do spraw Cyfryzacji) that reviews draft government digital documents; ran the review of the draft model AI contract clauses (comments due 20 February 2026; on the 27 February 2026 meeting agenda) and oversees implementation of the AI Policy.

organizations.name: Personal Data Protection Office
organizations.ai_governance_role: Polish data protection authority (UODO); published initial question lists on GDPR compliance for AI systems (August 2026) and is consulted under the AI systems Act on personal-data matters in the regulatory sandbox.

organizations.name: Polish Financial Supervision Authority
organizations.ai_governance_role: Financial supervisor (KNF, Office UKNF); issued recommendations on the impact of frontier AI models on financial-sector cybersecurity under DORA (July 2026); represented on KRiBSI under the AI systems Act.

organizations.name: Prime Minister of Poland
organizations.ai_governance_role: Head of government; sets the statutes of ministries, including the 2026 creation of an AI department in the Ministry of Digital Affairs.

organizations.name: Ministry of Education and Science
organizations.ai_governance_role: Ministry of Education and Science (Ministerstwo Edukacji i Nauki, 2020-2023); set up the 'AI w Edukacji' working group and published teacher guidance on ChatGPT and generative AI in schools in 2023.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Poland's official journals, the digital affairs ministry and the Council of Ministers, ministries and regulators were checked. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for transparency, standards, readiness indices, international agreements or historical publications. Not yet verified from the official text: material from the finance, labour and interior ministries, the competition, communications and broadcasting regulators, the national AI portal and the standards catalogue, which remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. ai.gov.pl JavaScript-only (guide PDF read from gov.pl). Finance, labour and interior ministries not searched one by one; UOKiK, UKE and KRRiT not searched directly; PKN catalogue unreachable. KRiBSI chair appointment (M.P. 2026 poz. 945-946) not logged as an event. Convention 108: Dz.U. 2003 nr 3 poz. 25, recorded on the COE file. Units covered: Law: Dziennik Ustaw and Monitor Polski searched via eli.gov.pl / Sejm ELI API: Act of 3 July 2026 on AI systems (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1003, AI Act implementation, KRiBSI, sandbox) read in full; KRiBSI chair appointment resolutions (M.P. 2026 poz. 945-946); 2020 AI Policy resolution (M.P. 2021 poz. 23). No other AI-titled acts, no deepfake-specific offence found by title search.; Government: Ministry of Digital Affairs (AI Policy to 2030 draft + ID260 draft resolution, AI guide for public administration), Committee for Digital Affairs (model AI clauses), Council of Ministers (2020 AI Policy). ai.gov.pl is a JavaScript app and could not be read; documents taken from gov.pl instead.; Ministries: Defence (AI strategy to 2039, recorded). Education, health, justice: searched, no official AI-specific ministry document found (education AI content is being added to core curricula from 1 Sept 2026 per a ministry reply, not an AI governance document). Finance/tax, labour, interior: not searched individually.; Regulators: UODO (AI GDPR question lists, recorded), KNF/UKNF (frontier-AI cybersecurity recommendations, recorded; 2020 robo-advice position kept as lead). PKN standards catalogue not reachable (ISO/IEC 42001 PN adoption unconfirmed). UOKiK, UKE, KRRiT, NASK/CERT Polska: one combined search, nothing AI-specific found.. Not reached: Ministries of finance, labour, interior (individual AI documents not searched); UOKiK, UKE, KRRiT sites not searched directly; PKN catalogue (standards) not reachable; ai.gov.pl portal (JavaScript-only, content not readable). Could not verify: ai.gov.pl guide page (JS-only; guide PDF read from gov.pl attachment instead); PN-ISO/IEC 42001 adoption by PKN; Convention 108+ ratification act Dz.U. 2019 poz. 2284 not opened (title only). transparency, standards, index-readiness, international, historical: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (coverage_audit.no_material_found_note): The finance, labour and interior ministries and the competition, communications and broadcasting regulators were not searched individually, and the national AI portal and the standards catalogue were unavailable, so these remain to be checked.

leads.title: Uchwała Rady Ministrów w sprawie ustanowienia „Polityki rozwoju sztucznej inteligencji w Polsce do 2030 roku”
leads.english_title: Council of Ministers resolution establishing the Policy for the Development of AI in Poland until 2030
leads.note: Draft resolution ID260 (15 April 2026) is in the opinion/agreement stage; once published in Monitor Polski, update i-3876c7f4f3d4 to national_strategy/adopted and mark Resolution No. 196 of 2020 superseded. 2026-10-22: Ministry of Digital Affairs project page 'Projekt uchwały Rady Ministrów w sprawie ustanowienia „Polityki rozwoju sztucznej inteligencji w Polsce do 2030 roku”' (ID260), first published 16.04.2026, carries the draft resolution, the Policy annex, justification and OSR (all dated 15.04.2026) plus consultation and opinion letters: https://www.gov.pl/web/cyfryzacja/projekt-uchwaly-rady-ministrow-w-sprawie-ustanowienia-polityki-rozwoju-sztucznej-inteligencji-w-polsce-do-2030-roku-id260 . The page does not state adoption by the Council of Ministers; keep as lead until the resolution appears in Monitor Polski. Consider linking this April 2026 draft version to the existing 2025-11-17 Policy record (attachment PDFs could not be read this pass).

leads.title: Polityka Cyfrowej Transformacji Edukacji (2024)
leads.note: MEN reply letter DKO-WPP.053.8.2025.MM dated 'Warszawa, 24 lipca 2025 r.' states the PCTE (2024) names AI as one of ten focus areas (curriculum updates, teacher training). The policy text itself was not located on an official page; check gov.pl/web/edukacja for the PCTE document and whether its AI pillar meets the strategy scope test. 2026-11-07: MEN consultation page dated 06.08.2024 (https://www.gov.pl/web/edukacja/polityka-cyfrowej-transformacji-edukacji---projekt-uchwaly-rady-ministrow-skierowany-do-konsultacji2): draft Council of Ministers resolution, comments by 28 August; AI is one of ten areas ('nowe technologie, w tym sztuczna inteligencja w szkole'), not a dedicated pillar. 2025 reports mention a new draft resolution; no adopted Monitor Polski text found. Keep as lead.
